diagnostics.alpha_sweep_note: Smooth, monotonic, converged trend (not solver noise) -- consistent with the wing wake sheet's position relative to the fixed-height stab shifting with base alpha, not a numerical artifact.
diagnostics.wake_convergence_note: Converged to <0.2 MAC points; not under-resolved.
diagnostics.tail_height_note: Raising the stab 1.5 ft (toward the wing's Z) made CMa MORE destabilizing, not less -- opposite the a-priori guess, but it proves strong sensitivity to tail height (i.e. wake proximity, not a reference bug, drives the result); the wake sheet likely sits near/at the wing's height band at this alpha.
diagnostics.panel_vs_vlm_note: Two independent solution methods agree to within 0.6 MAC points -- not a VLM-specific implementation artifact.
diagnostics.wing_alone_note: Untapered wing lands at 24.1% MAC, matching the textbook quarter-chord AC (~25%) and confirming the MAC/reference pipeline is correct. The actual params wing (taper 0.65, zero LE sweep) lands at 14.5% -- a real ~10-point forward AC shift from taper with an unswept LE (the c/4 line sweeps forward going outboard), not a bug.
diagnostics.verdict: SM=-3.5% MAC at the rotation-AoA condition is real, not a script or reference artifact. It compounds three genuine effects: (1) taper 0.65 with zero LE sweep shifts the isolated wing's own AC ~10 MAC points forward of the quarter-MAC assumption seaez/sizing.py's V_h/V_v hand calc relies on; (2) the stab loses real effectiveness to wing-wake proximity at this alpha (confirmed by cross-solver agreement and height sensitivity); (3) the hull fuselage adds ~2.5 further MAC points of destabilization. seaez/sizing.py has no downwash term and assumes AC=quarter-MAC, so its +11.5% SM oracle is optimistic for this short-coupled, low-tail layout.
